Options: front expiry 2026-11-20 straddle 14.4%, event-implied move 7.1% net of ordinary vol, ATM IV 123%, 25d skew +1.1 vol pts (balanced), put/call OI 0.2 (baseline, 2026-11-13). Run-up: -6.2% over 20 days, -75% from the 52-week high, and -34% since 2026-10-02, which tracks a sector rout (SOXX -24%, LITE -45%, AAOI -57%, COHR -35% over the same span, own arithmetic on Yahoo bars). Valuation: about 173M shares (Jane Street 13G/A filed 2026-11-12: 13.3M = 7.7%) x $5.10 = about $880M market cap against $796M cash and short-term investments at Q2 end (Q2 release, 2026-08-13), so enterprise value is roughly $100-150M after a quarter of burn: the stock trades close to cash. Consensus Q3 revenue is scattered across aggregators at $0.97M-$3.1M (vs $0.57M in Q2), EPS about -$0.06/-0.07; one or two analysts, MarketBeat consensus 'Sell', $8 average target. Guide: 'optical engine production ramp on schedule for 2H 2026', 'begin shipping substantial numbers of production units for qualification in the remaining quarters of 2026', >30,000 engines targeted for 2026 (company FAQ 2026-07-14). Short interest about 14% of float, 3.2 days (through 2026-10-09). Release 07:00 ET Monday, no call this quarter; new CFO from 2026-11-02. Last real print (Q2, 2026-08-13 bmo) moved +0.45% on the day.
view: POET is a pre-revenue optical-interposer company whose quarterly revenue (sub-$1M) is irrelevant to a valuation that already sits near its cash pile. The print can only move the stock through the release's narrative: whether 800G engine shipments under the >$5M systems-integrator order and qualification units actually started in Q3/Q4, any new order, and Lumilens sample timing. The company promised 'additional announcements and updates in September' in the Q2 release and none of substance came (only a CIOE exhibit notice on 2026-09-04); the 2026-11-02 CFO release still speaks of moving 'into volume production', so Q3 revenue probably lands at the low end of an incoherent consensus, as Q2 did (miss vs about $0.65M). That leans slightly negative on the headline. Against it: a revenue miss on a $1-3M base has repeatedly produced small reactions (Q2 +0.45%, Q4-2024 about -3%), the stock is near cash with 14% short interest and a retail following that bids any order news, and the release without a call will almost certainly restate 'on schedule' language. Over Friday close to Monday 13:00 ET, sector beta (semis fell 3.6% today and swung 10%+ days this month) is likely to dominate whatever the release says. I see no reaction the price does not already hold.

recommendation.reason: No dated evidence shows the ramp slipped or accelerated since the 2026-08-13 release; the only lean is a likely low revenue print against scattered $1-3M estimates, which this stock has historically shrugged off. Near-cash valuation and 14% short interest cushion the downside, and Monday's sector tape will likely swamp the release. Not a bet I would make.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An explicit statement that 800G production shipments or customer qualification slipped into 2027 (bearish, likely beyond the 7% implied move), or a new named production order / Lumilens sample shipment (bullish, retail squeeze).

self_critique: The strongest case against neutrality is that a company that skipped its promised September update, changed CFO weeks before the release and declined to hold a call is preparing to disclose a slip into 2027, which in a sector rout could take the stock well below cash-adjusted levels. The opposite case: a near-cash stock with 14% short interest needs only one named production order in the release to rip 15-20%. Both tails are real and I cannot see which the release holds.
approach_notes: P4 and the sector check (own arithmetic on peer bars) helped most: it showed the October fall was beta, not an unpriced company problem. P3's worker/customer routes had little to work with for a sub-$1M-revenue foreign issuer with no call.
